🌳 When to plant gum arabic (acacia) in Nigeria

Also called Ɗakwara (Hausa).

Quick answer: Plant gum arabic (acacia) in Nigeria from July to August and harvest from November to March. Trees are tapped after the rains and the gum is collected in the dry season.

PlantJuly to August
HarvestNovember to March
Grows inNorth-East and North-West
TypeTree & cash crops
Local namesƊakwara

About gum arabic (acacia)

Acacia trees produce gum arabic and also help stop desert spread in the far north.

How to plant gum arabic (acacia) well

Collect clean, light-coloured gum lumps for the best price.

Trees are tapped after the rains and the gum is collected in the dry season.

Diseases and pests of gum arabic (acacia)

  • Termites on seedlingsProtect young seedlings and water them during dry spells.
  • Over-tappingTap correctly so trees recover.

Best states for gum arabic (acacia)

Borno · Yobe · Jigawa · Bauchi · Gombe · Adamawa · Kano · Katsina · Sokoto · Zamfara

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant gum arabic (acacia) in Nigeria?

Plant gum arabic (acacia) in Nigeria from July to August and harvest from November to March. Trees are tapped after the rains and the gum is collected in the dry season.

What is gum arabic (acacia) called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

Gum arabic (Acacia) is called Ɗakwara (Hausa).

When is gum arabic (acacia) harvested in Nigeria?

Gum arabic (Acacia) is usually harvested from November to March.

Which Nigerian states grow the most gum arabic (acacia)?

Borno, Yobe, Jigawa, Bauchi, Gombe, Adamawa, Kano, Katsina, Sokoto and Zamfara are among the best-known gum arabic (acacia) states.

Can I grow gum arabic (acacia) in my part of Nigeria?

Gum arabic (Acacia) grows best in the North-East and North-West regions. In other regions, ask your ADP extension officer before planting.

What diseases attack gum arabic (acacia) and how do I prevent them?

Termites on seedlings: Protect young seedlings and water them during dry spells. Over-tapping: Tap correctly so trees recover.
